title: A.X K2 serving re-measurement protocol on 2 x ND96amsr A100 v4 (vLLM v0.23.0)
status: Pre-registration draft. The screening ran once at main 5dc653b; its follow-ups (the mp-multinode C4m, C8m, C16m and the PD rerun) and the rounds have not run. The screening (section screen) picks the round candidates first; then freeze aml/src/bench/ (this file, slo_suites.py, protocol.sh, bench_stats.py, lb_proxy.py, node_tools.py, nixl_preflight.py) and docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md in one commit with the chosen ROUND_LAYOUTS before round 1; publish every run, including invalid and aborted runs.
assumptions: The SLO tiers are assumptions until the customer agrees them (or supplies its own) before round 1.

The common --max-model-len of 131072 must be at least the customer's longest input plus output and at most C2's auto-fitted 238,656 tokens; if the customer needs 262,144 tokens, C2 leaves the candidate list.
Prices change; pull the Azure retail prices again on the publication date.

nvfp4.requires: NVFP4_SM80_PORT=1 (applied by apply_overlay.py at job start)

server.prefix_caching: on (the production default); every measured point starts idle, after POST /reset_prefix_cache, and fails its gate if more than 1% of the queried prompt tokens hit the cache
server.eager_fallback: forbidden: a comparison phase that does not start with CUDA graphs fails; it is never retried with --enforce-eager
server.transport: FP8 two-node phases need NCCL over InfiniBand: the phase fails when the IB probe did not choose IB or any communicator used NET/Socket
notes: --max-num-seqs and --max-num-batched-tokens are per engine; C2 (DP2) therefore has twice A's system-wide budget, which C2s halves.
--api-server-count 1 removes C2's default of two API servers; --async-scheduling and the CUDA graph mode pin what vLLM 0.23 otherwise chooses.

dp_ep_batch_rule.rule: A two-node FP8 DP x EP layout shares C2's total batch budget of 16,384 tokens: per engine 16,384 / DP (C2 8,192, C4 4,096, C8 2,048, C16 1,024). NVFP4: D8 1,024, D24 8,192. A sensitivity layout (C2s, C4s, ...) keeps its own definition: total 8,192 (A's), per engine 8,192 / DP.
dp_ep_batch_rule.reason: With all2all_backend allgather_reducescatter, vLLM 0.23 gathers every DP rank's tokens per MoE forward without chunking, so the profile run sizes the Marlin MoE workspace for M = DP x max_num_batched_tokens tokens (about 229,376 bytes per token in BF16). At 8,192 tokens per engine C8 would leave about 19K KV tokens per engine and C16 and D8 would run out of memory.

launchers.note: How a layout's server starts. Default: one vllm serve on node0 (Ray places a two-node layout's workers on node1; a phase with replicas starts a second server on node1 through the bench replica actor). A layout with "launcher": "mp-multinode" uses the launch below.

mp-multinode.description: vLLM's documented multi-node data parallelism without Ray (docs/serving/data_parallel_deployment.md:37-47 of v0.23.0): node0 serves the single API endpoint and DP ranks 0..L-1; node1 runs ranks L..DP-1 headless and connects to node0's address and RPC port
mp-multinode.api_only_note: Node1 gets every flag of node0 except these API-server flags, plus peer_args. --reasoning-parser stays on both nodes: vLLM 0.23 passes it to the engine (StructuredOutputsConfig and ReasoningConfig, vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:610, 2171-2177, 2441-2445). --headless rejects --api-server-count above 0 (vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py); node0 never gets --data-parallel-start-rank, which would switch it to hybrid load balancing.

placeholders.@head_ip: node0's address, the same value on both nodes

mp-multinode.order: node0 first, node1 within seconds after it (a remote engine waits about 5 minutes for the head's reply to its HELLO). Only node0's /health is awaited: the head answers once every DP engine of both nodes has connected. Node1's process is checked every minute, so the wait ends when it exits.
mp-multinode.relaunch: A length fallback stops and relaunches both nodes with -1; vLLM's KV-capacity error may appear in either node's log (node0's log, node1's log tail).
mp-multinode.stop: node1's process group (bench replica stop), then node0's session, every time; the clean-state checks cover both nodes

ray_dp_failure.measured: Screening at main 5dc653b: C4, C8 and C16 (Ray DP backend, two or more engines per node) failed about 70 s after start in RayWorkerProc.initialize_worker -> ncclCommInitRank with NCCL error 'invalid usage'. C2 (Ray DP, one engine per node) and D8, D24 (mp DP, several engines on one node) passed.
ray_dp_failure.inferred: Verified by elimination in NCCL 2.28.9: the only ncclInvalidUsage path of ncclCommInitRank left is the duplicate-GPU check (src/init.cc:903-907). Likely: the DP group is the first communicator joining two engines of one node, and both engines' workers bound the same GPUs because RayExecutorV2 rewrites CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES in running workers (vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py:368-397). The exact trigger is unknown.
ray_dp_failure.consequence: The same topologies run as C4m, C8m and C16m with this launcher; the Ray variants and their failed results stay as they are.

PD.description: NVFP4 prefill/decode disaggregation over NixlConnector (experimental): a prefill server (D, kv_producer) on node0 and a decode server (D, kv_consumer) on node1 behind lb_proxy.py --prefill/--decode on node0
PD.diagnosis: Screening (main 5dc653b): scr-PD failed at start in register_kv_caches with NIXL_ERR_BACKEND, 'VRAM memory is detected as host by UCX'. The image's nixl-cu12 1.2.0 bundles UCX 1.21.0 built with CUDA, so no rebuild is needed. Remaining causes: a miss of UCX's memory-type cache (fix: UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n) or a zero-length KV descriptor from the SM80 port (UCX types a zero-length registration as host memory). UCX's CUDA module failing to load is unlikely: the logs have no 'UCX CUDA support was not found' warning.
PD.preflight: Before the servers start, nixl_preflight.py registers VRAM through NIXL on node0 and node1, once with the defaults and once with UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n, each run 120 s at most (node0.<phase>.preflight). The servers get the defaults if they pass on both nodes, else UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n if that passes on both; otherwise the phase records 'PD not possible here: NIXL preflight failed (<reason>)' and does not start. UCX_TLS is never set: it would drop InfiniBand.
PD.debug_relaunch: When the preflight passed and the launch still fails with 'VRAM memory is detected as host', both servers relaunch once with VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG; their 'Registering descs' lines and any zero-length descriptor go to node0.<phase>.failure, and the phase stops without suites.
PD.note: vLLM 0.23 deprecates kv_role kv_both for NixlConnector (docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md); the proxy follows tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py of v0.23.0. NIXL moves the KV cache over UCX, not NCCL: node0's InfiniBand counters per point show where it went. Each server sets VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST to its own node address at start.

phase_templates.note: PHASE_PLAN tokens <kind>-<layout> for a layout without an explicit phase (round candidates chosen by the screening): slo- (slo-sensitivity for a sensitivity layout), cap-, dx1-, dx2- and scr-. Explicit phases win; experimental layouts get none.

rounds.design: A -> the candidates in the round's order -> (sensitivity runs in round 1) -> A2 -> (capacity phases in round 1); the A baseline of a round is the geometric mean of A and A2 for the metrics both launches measured
rounds.layouts_rule: The candidates compared with A: ROUND_LAYOUTS (comma-separated, printed by `bench_stats.py select` from the screening) or this list. Odd rounds run them in the listed order, even rounds in reverse (C2,D: round 1 C2 then D, round 2 D then C2). Fix ROUND_LAYOUTS before round 1 and keep it for every round; rounds 4 and 5 run only if the extension rule fires.
rounds.sensitivity: <X>s for every candidate X that has a sensitivity layout (C2s, C4s, C8s, C16s, C4ms, C8ms, C16ms): X's per-engine limits divided by its DP size, so its system-wide budget equals A's
rounds.capacity: cap-A and cap-<X> for every candidate X
rounds.allocations: Each round is a separate job. Round 3 must run on a different node pair (compare the hashed host names); rounds 1 and 2 may share one.

R.description: Part R: replay of the published 1K/8K/32K x concurrency 1 and 32 matrix

S1.description: W1 lengths at fixed concurrency (closed loop)

W1real.description: W1 lengths with real Korean and English text (aml/src/bench/parity_corpus.json windows, or the customer's JSONL)

soak.description: W1 at 0.8 x lambda* of the standard SLO for 45 minutes (soak round only)

warmup.description: discarded: one 32-request burst per input length, 64 output tokens, then a cache reset

sampling.never: --num-warmups (it resends prompt 0, which then hits the prefix cache)

slo.assumption: ASSUMPTION: agree these tiers (or the customer's own) before round 1.
slo.definition: lambda* = the highest arrival rate at which at least 90% of the steady-state requests (by start time) meet both the TTFT and the TPOT limit; failed requests count as misses

seeds.point: index of the point in its workload's full list (rate grid or Part R list), so subsets keep their seeds
seeds.rerun: an invalid point is rerun once with the same seed (common random numbers) after a cache reset
seeds.rate_order_formula: 1000000*ROUND + 10000*WORKLOAD + 99 seeds a shuffle of the grid indices; the same order for every layout

p1.long_documents_last: the two 32K documents run in suite paritylong, after the performance points

acceptance_fp8.early_divergence: a first difference before token 16 on more than 2 of the 32 greedy prompts means the layout is misconfigured

parity.nvfp4: report the differences against A; quality equivalence needs the separate accuracy subset (KoBALT 200 + CLIcK 300, paired McNemar, non-inferiority margin -3 points)

gates.preemptions: a point with preemptions is marked capacity-bound, not invalid
gates.kv_bound: a point whose peak KV usage on any engine is >= 0.95, or whose closed-loop peak of running requests stays below its concurrency, is marked KV-bound and kept out of speed decisions

throttle.note: Invalid: HW slowdown (0x8), SW thermal (0x20), HW thermal (0x40), HW power brake (0x80). SW power cap (0x4) is the normal operating limit of a loaded A100 and is reported per point, not invalidating; 02-bench-audit c.5 proposed idle-only.

gates.round: a round counts only if every planned point of every planned phase has a valid attempt; never use a round in part

statistics.steady_state: requests whose start time falls in the workload window; output tok/s counts the per-token timestamps (start + TTFT + cumulative ITL) inside the window

bootstrap.method: moving blocks of consecutive requests spanning 30 s of arrivals

lambda_star.interpolation: linear between the last grid rate that meets the threshold and the next one

statistics.next_grid: after round 1, four rates from 0.6 x to 1.4 x lambda* (geometric), per workload, shared by every layout when one grid brackets all of them

decision_rules.comparison: for metric M and round k, r_k = ln(M_X,k / M_base,k); M_base,k = sqrt(M_A,k x M_A2,k) when A2 measured M, else M_A,k; report exp(mean r) and exp(mean +- t_975(n-1) x sd / sqrt(n)) plus the min and max over rounds
better: the 95% CI of the ratio excludes 1
decision_rules.delta_min: max(ln 1.05, 2 x max_k |ln(A2_k / A_k)|) of the same metric; for metrics A2 did not measure, the largest such value over the metrics it did measure
decision_rules.equivalent: the whole 95% CI of the ratio lies in [0.95, 1.05]

extend.rule: add rounds (up to 5) when the SD over rounds of ln(A2/A) exceeds 2% for any overlapping primary metric or a primary metric's 95% CI half-width exceeds 5%

decision_rules.a2_limitation: A2 runs start-up, warm-up, Part R and two W1 rates only, so drift correction applies to those metrics; lambda*, W2 and cost use A alone
ranking: cost per 1M output tokens at lambda*

prices_usd_per_node_hour.region: uksouth, Linux, Standard_ND96amsr_A100_v4 (Azure retail prices as recorded in evidence/a100-nvfp4-single-node.json)
prices_usd_per_node_hour.note: Low-priority capacity has been billed at the Spot rate since 2026-03-31; the older 8.19 low-priority rate no longer applies. Refresh every price before publishing.

dx2.pass: lambda*(Dx2) >= 1.9 x lambda*(Dx1) for W1 and W2 at the standard SLO

proxy.policy: least outstanding requests, ties in round-robin order

pairs.name: A1: indexer grid scales with max_model_len
DCP: KV capacity and speed of TP16 with DCP 2

diagnostics.dcp_rule: DCP counts as supported only if diag-B0dcp starts, its KV tokens clearly exceed diag-B0's, the DCP group lines appear, parity against diag-A holds and the short load completes

screen.description: Screening before the rounds: one launch of every A100-feasible layout records start facts, short parity against the job's first launch, Part R and Poisson W1; every step and every phase fails softly (recorded, the job goes on)
screen.seeds: ROUND 0 of the seed formula (10000*WORKLOAD + 100*POINT): the same prompts for every layout, apart from every round
screen.order: Each job runs its reference first and the layouts expected to fail or to relaunch with -1 last (C16 and B0dcp in the FP8 job, C16m in the FP8 DP job, D8 in the NVFP4 job, PD in the two-node job), so a node they leave dirty cannot spoil a healthy phase.
screen.reference_rule: parity reference = the job's first launch: scr-A (both FP8 jobs), scr-D (NVFP4 job), scr-Dx1 (two-node NVFP4 job), scr-Dref (the PD rerun job)
screen.steps_option: a phase's options.screen.steps runs a subset of the steps: scr-Dref (D on node0) records start facts and parity only, the light parity reference of the PD rerun
screen.facts: seconds to healthy, the served max_model_len (/v1/models), KV tokens per engine (vllm:cache_config_info and every 'GPU KV cache size' log line), the requested and fitted length after a length fallback

parity.note: Loose on purpose: it catches a broken or misconfigured layout, not small numeric differences; the rounds apply the A2-based acceptance. Through PD, P1 (prompt_logprobs) reaches the prefill server alone; P2 runs the whole prefill -> KV transfer -> decode path.

partr.points: every Part R point at the published lengths (1,024 output tokens)
partr.capacity_note: 32 requests of 32K tokens with 64 output tokens record running requests, KV usage and preemptions only (a capacity point, never a speed number)

w1.note: W1 point p1 at 0.6 req/s (the grid's second rate): 360 s of arrivals, steady window 60-360 s

ladders.use: scr-Dx1 runs the W1 ladder, scr-Dx2 and scr-PD the dx2 ladder, instead of the single W1 point

screen.length_fallback: A screening server that cannot hold the common --max-model-len (vLLM: 'larger than the available KV cache memory') is relaunched once with -1; the requested and fitted lengths are recorded and the layout cannot join the rounds

selection.rule: A always. FP8: the eligible layout other than A with the highest R/isl8192-c32 output tok/s. NVFP4: the eligible one-node layout (D included) with the highest R/isl8192-c32 output tok/s. D x 2: when lambda*(W1, standard SLO) of scr-Dx2 >= 1.9 x that of scr-Dx1. Exact ties go to the layout listed first. A KV-bound or capacity-bound flag at the ranking point is reported next to the score with the peak KV usage and the peak of running requests; it never excludes a layout.
eligible: the phase passed (healthy start, effective-config and NCCL gates, the screen completed)
it held the common --max-model-len (no length fallback)
its short parity passed against the job's reference
the ranking point is valid (a KV-bound or capacity-bound flag there is reported, not excluded)
each listed c1 TPOT is at most tpot_max_ratio x the reference's
selection.same_job_reference: A candidate's reference (short parity and c1 TPOT) is the reference launch of its own job. A phase found in more than one package (scr-A of both FP8 jobs) is reported once per job, the later ones as <phase>@<job>, and every instance of a candidate phase competes.
selection.kv_bound_note: R/isl8192-c32 holds 32 x 9,216 = 294,912 tokens. D, E and Err (about 232K-254K KV tokens) and B0 (about 310K; peak KV usage 0.953 in the October run) are always KV-bound there, so the flag cannot exclude a layout or D, E and Err could never be chosen.

dx2.unbracketed: a lambda* outside its ladder is a bound; when the bounds cannot decide, the D x 2 job (slo-nvfp4-2replica-nd96.yml) decides with full grids

selection.pd: experimental: reported (lambda*, parity, preflight, failures, InfiniBand bytes), never selected in this protocol version. The PD rerun job has no Dx1 or Dx2: PD's pairs then take them from the earlier two-node job and are labelled cross-job.
selection.output: ROUND_LAYOUTS=<FP8 choice>,<NVFP4 choice> for slo-round-nd96.yml; round 1 adds <X>s when the FP8 choice has a sensitivity layout

pairs.name: A1: indexer grid scales with max_model_len

estimates.status: ESTIMATES, not measurements: model shape plus the evidence below; the screening records the real weights, KV tokens and fitted lengths
estimates.formula: weights per GPU = (routed experts / EP + shared experts (whole on every rank when sequence-parallel MoE applies: DP > 1, TP > 1, EP; whole anyway at TP1) + TP-sharded non-expert / TP + replicated non-expert) x (layers of the worst pipeline stage / 61); KV tokens per engine = (0.9 x 80 GiB - weights - other) / (1,284 B x layers per GPU)
estimates.kv_bytes_note: bf16 MLA latent 1,152 B + DSA indexer key 132 B, replicated on every TP rank; the ported TRITON_MLA_SPARSE backend has no FP8 KV cache (auto/fp16/bf16 only)

other_gib.note: activations, CUDA graphs and buffers, from the evidence: TP/PP about 3 (A), NVFP4 TP8 about 6.6 (D); DP x EP layouts add the Marlin MoE workspace of M = DP x max_num_batched_tokens tokens (server.dp_ep_batch_rule)

estimates.source: C4, C8, C16, D8, D24 and B0dcp: launch check of the screening layouts against the vLLM v0.23.0 source, at the per-engine batch sizes of server.dp_ep_batch_rule

C16.expected: relaunched with -1, so not a round candidate; its numbers are reported anyway

C4m.kv_tokens_per_engine: about 216K (as C4: the launcher does not change memory)

C16m.kv_tokens_per_engine: about 82K (as C16; D8's measured 32,896 against about 46K predicted suggests lower)
C16m.expected: relaunched with -1 on both nodes, so not a round candidate; its numbers are reported anyway

D8.expected: relaunched with -1, so not a round candidate; its numbers are reported anyway

reporting.primary: Every protocol job packages its own results (bench_stats.py package --report) after each phase and on exit, and reports them through report.py as chunked MLflow tags: the parts slo.package.<launch> (that launch's points) first, then slo.package (everything but the points, with each part's launch). Workspace storage is private and the workspace has no CPU cluster, so this in-job path is primary; collect-slo-outputs.yml is a fallback.
reporting.missing_part: a part that never arrived invalidates only the launch it holds
reporting.best_effort: bounded with timeout, never changes the job's exit status
